summary: On node1 (CentOS Stream 10), added fstab entries mounting /tmp and /dev/shm as tmpfs with nosuid,nodev,noexec. Verified live effect, then rebooted node1 and confirmed the boot_id changed and the mount options persisted across reboot, with functional proof that execution and setuid are blocked on both mounts post-reboot.
actions_performed: Inspected initial state: /dev/shm was tmpfs with nosuid,nodev only; /tmp was part of root xfs filesystem (no isolation), tmp.mount unit present but disabled
Backed up /etc/fstab, then appended two lines: 'tmpfs /tmp tmpfs defaults,nosuid,nodev,noexec 0 0' and 'tmpfs /dev/shm tmpfs defaults,nosuid,nodev,noexec 0 0'
Ran systemctl daemon-reload, remounted /dev/shm and mounted /tmp live to apply noexec,nosuid,nodev immediately
Captured pre-restart baseline: boot_id 984a7d52-3387-4830-a06e-15e8b5e6c2a1, findmnt showing both mounts healthy with hardened options
Rebooted node1 via systemctl reboot (backgrounded so the ack returned before disconnect)
Polled node1 until exec was available again; confirmed new boot_id c9102ed6-bd24-46f2-bfa3-bab32ddf3bc6, proving an actual restart occurred
Post-restart, re-verified findmnt output for /tmp and /dev/shm still shows nosuid,nodev,noexec, proving persistence via /etc/fstab
Functionally proved noexec/setuid enforcement post-reboot: attempted to execute a script in /tmp and a copied binary in /dev/shm; both failed with Permission denied / exit 126

evidence.requirement: /tmp and /dev/shm mounted with noexec, nosuid, nodev (program execution, setuid bits, device nodes ignored)
evidence.summary: Live mount output showed rw,nosuid,nodev,noexec,seclabel for both /dev/shm and /tmp immediately after configuration, confirmed again via findmnt

Captured pre-reboot baseline (boot_id 984a7d52...) with both mounts hardened, issued systemctl reboot, polled until node1 responded with new boot_id c9102ed6..., then re-ran findmnt showing /tmp and /dev/shm still mounted with nosuid,nodev,noexec after the restart

evidence.requirement: Functional proof that execution/setuid is actually blocked, not just flagged
evidence.summary: Post-reboot, attempting to execute a script placed in /tmp and a binary copied into /dev/shm both failed with 'Permission denied' and exit code 126

evidence.requirement: Mandatory node-restart evidence protocol (boot identity + service/data health before and after restart)
evidence.summary: Boot_id captured before (984a7d52-3387-4830-a06e-15e8b5e6c2a1) and after (c9102ed6-bd24-46f2-bfa3-bab32ddf3bc6) reboot differ, proving a genuine restart; connection timeouts/reset during the gap show the node was actually down; post-restart findmnt shows recovered, hardened mount state
